# Popular DEs and WMs: GNOME, KDE Plasma, i3, sway

Choosing the default graphical experience defines the outward personality of your distribution. The ecosystem broadly divides into **Full Desktop Environments (DEs)** and **Tiling Window Managers / Compositors (WMs)**.

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|               Desktop Interface Comparison                |
|                                                           |
| Category              Desktop Environments    Tiling WMs  |
| --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Examples              GNOME, KDE Plasma       i3, Sway    |
| Memory Footprint      ~600 MB - 1.2 GB RAM    ~60 MB RAM  |
| Window Management     Floating / Overlapping  Tiled Grid  |
| Integrated Apps       File Manager, Settings, Minimal     |
|                       Terminal, Text Editor   (Bring your |
| Configuration Method  Graphical Control Panel Plaintext   |
| Primary Toolkit       GTK (GNOME) / Qt (KDE)  None / C    |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```

## GNOME 40+ (Mutter & GTK4)

GNOME is the default desktop environment for Fedora, Ubuntu, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux.
- **Architectural Philosophy:** Streamlined, opinionated user experience focused on virtual workspace workflow and distraction-free design.
- **Under the Hood:** Built on the `GTK4` toolkit and `libadwaita`. The window manager and Wayland compositor is **Mutter**. Configuration is stored centrally in the GSettings/dconf binary database.
- **Packaging Burden:** High. GNOME requires packaging dozens of interrelated libraries (`glib`, `gobject-introspection`, `tracker`, `mutter`, `gnome-shell`, `pipewire`).

## KDE Plasma 6 (KWin & Qt6)

KDE Plasma is known for modularity, customizability, and feature density.
- **Architectural Philosophy:** Extreme user control. Almost every aspect of the UI, panel layout, and keybindings can be customized.
- **Under the Hood:** Built entirely upon **Qt6** and **KDE Frameworks (KF6)**. The compositor is **KWin**, which provides high-performance Wayland compositing with fractional scaling and color management.

## i3 and Sway: Minimalist Tiling

For power users, developers, and lightweight appliances, tiling compositors replace floating windows with a deterministic grid:
- **`i3` (X11):** The classic, ultra-fast manual tiling window manager. Windows automatically arrange themselves in columns, rows, or tabbed splits.
- **`Sway` (Wayland):** A drop-in, modern replacement for i3 built on the **`wlroots`** modular Wayland library. It uses the exact same configuration syntax as i3, but runs natively under Wayland with hardware-accelerated rendering and modern touchpad gestures.
- **Packaging Burden:** Very low. Sway and wlroots compile in minutes with few dependencies, making them an ideal choice for a custom Linux distribution.
